item.title: Lemonade Completes Nationwide Renters Insurance Rollout
item.description: (Image source: IIR.) Lemonade (New York) has launched renters insurance in Minnesota, completing nationwide availability for the product across all 50 states and Washington, D.C. The expansion makes renters insurance the first Lemonade product offered throughout the United States. “From the start, we built Lemonade Renters to remove the complexity that makes traditional insurance frustrating, and to offer affordable coverage that renters can buy and manage on their own terms,” comments Dan Timsit, Head of Renters Insurance, Lemonade.

item.title: Google AI in School Triggered Teen’s Mental Health Crisis, Lawsuit Says
item.description: It scored significantly worse on safety than the previous generation of Google’s AI, responding appropriately to messages about mental health just 7% of the time, according to findings from the nonprofit research initiative KORA cited in the complaint. Parents in North Carolina sued Google after their 13-year-old daughter spent months discussing suicidal thoughts with the company’s artificial intelligence tools on her school-issued Chromebook, underscoring the potential risks of the technology as parents and educators debate AI’s place in schools. By the time the school notified her parents, she had been corresponding with Google about such topics for months, often using a feature in Google Search known as AI Mode.

item.title: Smiling Regularly May Be Good for Your Health
item.description: “It’s just like another thing that you can add to your toolbox.” Smiling can affect one’s level of cortisol, a hormone the body releases partly to help regulate stress and mood, according to Ho. Research backs up the fact that smiling goes a long way. “When you’re doing it in a room by yourself, you’re not doing it in a social interaction, maybe it’s making you remember, or it’s an effect of remembering some good thing that happened and that would put you in a better mood.” At the Orange County Academy of Sciences and Arts in Southern California, the power of a smile is taken very seriously.

item.title: American Jobs Offer More Autonomy — and More Stress
item.description: American jobs have become increasingly stressful over the past two decades—but workers have also gained greater ability to exercise independence and make decisions at work. Yet workers generally are not being paid more to compensate for the added stress, according to a working paper examining how the health-related characteristics of U.S. “What we found is that this evolution toward more stressful jobs is not due to the fact that workers are taking different jobs now than they did 20 or 25 years ago,” said study co-author Fabien Postel-Vinay, a research professor in SMU Department of Economics.

item.title: New Partnerships at Hippo, Donegal, Mitchell
item.description: Through the investment model of Greenlight Re Innovations, Hippo can invest alongside Greenlight Re in early-stage insurance programs, while its subsidiary Spinnaker Insurance Company can serve as Greenlight’s preferred U.S. The partnership comes as Hippo works with emerging MGA programs to support insurance innovation and diversify across insurance products. Greenlight Re brings a source of potential investments and program partners supported by Hippo’s underwriting experience and Spinnaker’s carrier capacity.

item.title: FCA acts to protect consumers facing demands for disguised remuneration scheme loan repayments
item.description: These follow demands it made for people to repay loans, or purported loans, provided as part of disguised remuneration schemes. Ethica is acting on behalf of West 28th Street Limited (West 28), which bought disguised remuneration loans from a third party. Disguised remuneration schemes saw people – often contractors, consultants and agency workers – paid for their work through loans instead of regular salaries.

item.title: Exclusive: Nurx And Journey Clinical Co-Founders Raise $6M For Mental Health Startup Siggy
item.description: Siggy has raised $6 million in pre-seed funding to build a mental health service that uses AI to collect patients’ histories and track progress between appointments with licensed clinicians, the startup told Crunchbase News exclusively. Jonathan Sabbagh co-founded Journey Clinical , which supports practices offering ketamine-assisted psychotherapy, and Edvard Engesæth co-founded Nurx , which provides birth control and other healthcare services online. The founders said they began building Siggy in late 2025.

item.title: Verisk’s 9M’26 revenue rises 4.5% to $2.398bn
item.description: Verisk’s revenues for the first nine months of 2026 rose 4.5% to $2.398 billion, up from $2.294 billion in the same period of 2025. Looking at Q3 2026 alone, the pattern was similar to the nine-month picture, with revenue and adjusted EBITDA both rising while net income declined. Lee Shavel, President and CEO, Verisk, commented, “Our strong third-quarter results underscore the resilience of our subscription-based business model and the mission-critical role Verisk plays in the insurance ecosystem.

item.title: Kin does not expect to tap reinsurance for Hurricane Isaias claims
item.description: US-based Kin, a direct-to-consumer provider of home insurance and home financing services, has indicated that claims arising from Hurricane Isaias are unlikely to require support from its reinsurance arrangements, with early loss experience broadly aligning with catastrophe model projections. The insurer anticipates approximately 1,350 claims from the October hurricane, with the majority originating in Florida’s Panhandle region. Isaias struck near Destin, Florida, on 9 October as a Category 2 hurricane, producing sustained winds of 105 mph.

item.title: Liberty Mutual’s net income declines 7% to $2.1bn in Q3’26 amid higher cat losses
item.description: Tim Sweeney, Liberty Mutual Chairman & Chief Executive Officer, said, “Liberty Mutual delivered another excellent quarter, generating $2.1 billion in net income and an 89.5% combined ratio. and its subsidiaries (collectively, LMHC) reported net income attributable to LMHC of $2.067 billion for the third quarter of 2026, a 7% decrease from $2.223 billion in the same period a year prior. Underlying pre-tax operating income (PTOI) before limited partnerships income stood at $1.901 billion, down 13.6% from $2.199 billion.

item.title: Confie Acquires Insurance Operations of TDECU
item.description: Confie has acquired the insurance operations of TDECU (Texas Dow Employees Credit Union), one of the largest credit unions in Texas. The TDECU insurance operations will become part of InsureOne, Confie’s standard and preferred personal lines agency and home to its growing credit union partnerships. The 34 employees who supported TDECU’s insurance operations will join InsureOne’s credit union division, providing continuity for TDECU members while gaining access to Confie’s broader carrier relationships, technology, and insurance capabilities.

item.title: Auto Insurer Root Reverses Q3 Loss Last Year With $14M Net Income
item.description: reported third quarter 2026 net income of $14.4 million, reversing a loss of $5.4 million over the same period a year ago. Still, Root said its partnership channel grew 19% in Q3 and represented 52% of new writings compared with 44% last year in Q3. “Vehicle buyers should not have to leave a high-intent purchase to complete a separate insurance process.” With Root’s expansion to New Jersey in July and Wyoming last month, the insurer is now in 38 states.

item.title: Missouri Releases Workers’ Comp Rates for 2027
item.description: The Missouri Department of Commerce and Insurance (DCI) announced the release of workers’ compensation rates for employers for 2027. The National Council on Compensation Insurance (NCCI) has proposed rate-neutral loss costs at 0%, keeping average rates steady for Missouri businesses. The NCCI’s 2027 loss cost filing and the department’s independent actuarial review are available on DCI’s website .

item.title: Record investment sales carry Primerica as term life slips
item.description: Primerica reported third-quarter 2026 revenue of $902 million, up 7% year over year, as record investment sales offset weaker term life insurance sales. Investment and Savings Products sales increased 19% to $4.4 billion. Term life insurance policies issued fell 7% to 73,813, while issued face amount declined 5% to $25.7 billion.

item.title: Zywave 2026 Fall Launch Connects Producers, Agencies and Carriers for Stronger Insurance Distribution
item.description: The post Zywave 2026 Fall Launch Connects Producers, Agencies and Carriers for Stronger Insurance Distribution appeared first on Coverager - Insurance news and insights . Producer Agent moves into Zywave Apex MCP, and new system connections help every renewal start ready Zywave today announced the second set of updates in its Fall 2026 Launch , helping producers win new business, agencies start every renewal ready, and carriers see how their distribution is performing. Zywave product experts will walk through the full Fall 2026 Launch in a webinar on November 11 at 12:00 p.m.

item.title: IA Capital announces initial close of Inter-Atlantic Opportunity Fund I
item.description: VC firm IA Capital Group announced the initial close of Inter-Atlantic Opportunity Fund I, its 11th fund. The Opportunity Fund targets what IA Capital sees as a widening gap in late-stage fintech and insurtech: as generalist and corporate investors have shifted their attention elsewhere, well-run companies with real revenue have fewer natural sources of growth capital and liquidity. IA Capital’s investment team, led by General Partner Ravi Shah, has closed two Opportunity Fund investments to date: Panacea, a US-based financial platform built for doctors, dentists and veterinarians and their practices, and Aurora, a UK-based algorithmic underwriting platform that automates P&C underwriting.

item.title: El ministro de Agricultura visita Agroseguro
item.description: Luis Planas, ministro de Agricultura, Pesca y Alimentación, ha visitado las oficinas de Agroseguro acompañado del presidente de ENESA, Ernesto Abati, y el director de la misma, Miguel Pérez Cimas.

item.title: Los jóvenes prefieren el trato presencial con su corredor de seguros
item.description: El IV Informe del Mediador de Seguros en España elaborado por Aegon señala que el 46,4% de la Generación Z (1997-2012) prefiere el trato presencial frente a otras opciones de contacto, 10,6 puntos porcentuales más que la media de las demás generaciones: Millenials (1981-1996), Generación X (1965-1980) y Boomers (1946-1964).

item.title: AIG’s General Insurance Q3 Underwriting Income Down 29%
item.description: Third-quarter 2026 underwriting income in American International Group’s (AIG) General Insurance segment decreased nearly 30% compared with the prior year, to $564 million. “Compared to the same nine-month period last year, we delivered double-digit top-line growth in premiums, exceeded $2 billion in underwriting income, and improved the combined ratio 140 basis points to 89.2.” Underwriting income in North America commercial was $167 million, down 57% compared with Q3 2025. The combined ratio for the General Insurance unit—which includes North America commercial, international commercial and global personal—was 91.3 compared with 86.8 last year.

item.title: When Claimants Use AI: How Insurers Can Adapt Their Workflows
item.description: Insureds’ growing use of generative artificial intelligence to submit claims and contest adverse determinations is challenging insurers’ claims management systems and protocols. For insurers, this increased use of gen AI by insureds creates a potential disruption to the traditional claim handling process in addition to increasing overall costs and workload. The challenge for insurers is to develop better workflow strategies without allowing the higher complexity or appearance of the paperwork to turn into higher loss adjustment expenses.

item.title: FCA to explore quantum computing to tackle financial crime
item.description: The FCA will bring together financial services firms, quantum technology providers and national research laboratories to explore how quantum computing could help tackle financial crime. The group will help firms explore practical uses of quantum computing in financial services and share findings to guide future testing. By bringing together firms, technology providers and researchers we can build readiness and identify practical applications for common industry challenges, starting with financial crime.' The initiative builds on the FCA’s research into the long-term potential of quantum computing in financial services .

item.title: Looking back to move forward: why reviewing our rules matters
item.description: Rules that were appropriate when they were introduced may need to be updated, simplified or, in some cases, removed altogether. That is why the FCA regularly reviews its rules. We also explore how rules are affecting firms, consumers and markets through our ongoing supervisory activities, data monitoring, market studies and calls for evidence.

item.title: Sector Snapshot: Construction Robotics Funding Soars To $1.6B, Tripling Previous Peak
item.description: San Francisco-based Bedrock Robotics , this year’s largest funding recipient in the sector, said in August that excavators equipped with its autonomous systems were operating without human operators on commercial projects in Texas and Nevada. Companies spanning construction and robotics have raised about $1.6 billion this year through Oct. The numbers: With roughly two months left in the year, funding has already surpassed the previous five years combined.

item.title: Swiss Re’s P&C reinsurance result delivers, despite competitive market weighing
item.description: Swiss Re has reported on-target results for its property and casualty (P&C) reinsurance division for the first nine months of this year, as lower than anticipated natural catastrophe losses and strong underwriting performance both served to offset the effects of the competitive and softened market environment. However, where competitive and softer reinsurance market conditions are most evident is in Swiss Re’s new business contractual service margin (CSM), which reflects the profitability of new business under written in the period. For P&C reinsurance this came in at $1.8 billion for Swiss Re, down meaningfully from $2.5 billion in the prior year, which the company said is reflective of “a competitive year-to-date market environment.” As we all know, the competition is likely to get even fiercer going forwards, while pricing is expected to soften further as well, meaning the profitability of new underwriting business will likely decline further across the reinsurance sector.

item.title: Selective returns for catastrophe bond renewal, with $300m High Point Re 2027-1
item.description: Selective Insurance Company is back in the catastrophe bond market for is second sponsorship, seeking $300 million or more in multi-peril collateralized reinsurance from a High Point Re Ltd. Selective Insurance, the US property and casualty insurer, had sponsored its debut catastrophe bond back in 2023, securing $300 million of protection from the High Point Re Ltd. However, this new High Point Re 2027-1 cat bond will include coverage for all 50 US states and DC, we understand, showing Selective’s expansion and desire to benefit from reinsurance across all exposed regions.

item.title: MS Amlin syndicate targets $100m aggregate retro with Kanata Re 2026-1 cat bond
item.description: The Kanata Re 2026-1 cat bond notes from Arthur Re are designed to provide Syndicate 2001 and sub-entities with a multi-year source of fully-collateralized multi-peril and multi-regional retrocessional reinsurance from the capital markets. Lloyd’s syndicate 2001, which is aligned with Mitsui Sumitomo underwriting entity MS Amlin, is seeking its first catastrophe bond protection, with a $100 million target for multi-peril and multi-regional retrocession from an Arthur Re Ltd. – Kanata Re 2026-1 cat bond sponsorship, Artemis has learned.

item.title: Verdant Rock names Thomas as CUO and adds two senior leaders
item.description: Verdant Rock Limited, a Bermuda Monetary Authority-regulated Class 3B insurance company, has appointed Carolyn Thomas as Chief Underwriting Officer (CUO), Kevin Downs as Chief Actuary, and Sarah Demerling as Global Head of Regulatory Affairs, effective 2 November 2026. In her new role, Thomas will lead Verdant Rock’s underwriting and will work with its origination and structuring team to build the insurer’s financial guarantee business. Most recently, she served at Aon Reinsurance Solutions, and advised clients on credit reinsurance and placed Verdant Rock’s first 30% quota share reinsurance treaty.

item.title: US cyber pricing stabilising, but tech risks and privacy claims loom: Howden Re
item.description: Pricing for US cyber insurance is stabilising after dropping for several years; however, claims from the 2023 underwriting year are still developing, while vulnerabilities are being discovered and exploited faster, Howden Re analysts highlight in a recent report. Rate softening has now entered its fourth year, and whilst Howden Re’s pricing data shows cyber rates continuing to soften, the pace of reduction has materially decelerated. “Coalescence in actual and expected RARC is a positive sign that the market is stabilising,” said Luke Foord-Kelcey, Global Head of Cyber at Howden Re.

item.title: RiverStone International enters into $325m LPT with Clear Spring
item.description: Global legacy acquirer RiverStone International has entered into a loss portfolio transfer (LPT) with Clear Spring Property and Casualty Company, a subsidiary of Delaware Life Insurance, covering approximately $325 million in net reserves. This announcement comes days after RiverStone International unveiled its ILS debut with an LPT of portfolios associated with funds managed by Leadenhall Capital Partners. The LPT with Clear Spring covers discontinued US workers’ compensation business from accident years 2018–2025, providing the P&C insurer with operational and economic finality for the discontinued portfolio.

item.title: Insurer FM Donates Rhode Island United Way’s Largest Gift in Its History
item.description: Commercial property insurer FM announced a $5 million gift from the FM Foundation to United Way of Rhode Island,. United Way of Rhode Island said FM’s gift will help expand its Family Stability Initiative, including opening additional economic empowerment centers that provide families with coordinated support designed to build long-term stability and resilience. The gift is the largest single corporate donation in the nonprofit organization’s history.

item.title: People Moves: SAN Group Names Chief Operating Officer; Radian Names Executives
item.description: SAN Group Names von Jess Chief Operating Officer SAN Group , headquartered in Hampton, New Hampshire, appointed Tom von Jess as chief operating officer. Stuart Bridges , a founder of Inigo who has served as its chief financial officer, will take on a new role as Radian group advisor, expanding Radian’s connections with key business partners and market participants, including P&C-focused investors. Dan Kobell was named chief financial officer, reporting to Radian CEO Mike Weinbach.

item.title: Police Clash With Protesters in French City of Lyon
item.description: French riot police fired tear gas and charged a group of protesters in the French city of Lyon on Thursday as demonstrations took place across the country in a renewed challenge to President Emmanuel Macron after weeks of unrest . Some of the protesters were seen shouting anti-police slogans and some were dressed all in black, with face coverings. French high school students and other demonstrators had earlier faced off against riot police in Paris as they blocked a street with rubbish bins on Thursday morning.

item.title: Munich Re Ventures-backed Sentra raises $150 million
item.description: Munich Re Ventures-backed Sentra has raised $150 million in a strategic investment led by Capital One Ventures. Other existing investors include Bessemer Venture Partners, Zeev Ventures, Standard Investments and Key1 Capital. Sentra says it analyzes data within customers’ environments without transferring it elsewhere.

item.title: Arity revenue rises 11.8% as Allstate expands mobility data business
item.description: Arity revenue rose 11.8% to $76 million, driven by higher lead generation advertising sales. Allstate reported third-quarter 2026 net income applicable to common shareholders of $2.05 billion, down 44.8% from a year earlier, as higher catastrophe losses and investment losses weighed on results. Revenue increased 0.5% to $17.35 billion.

item.title: Old Mutual Insure to take over Swiss Re’s South African insurance portfolio
item.description: Old Mutual Insure and Swiss Re Corporate Solutions announced a proposed cooperation that would transfer Swiss Re Corporate Solutions’ South African insurance portfolio to Old Mutual Insure, subject to regulatory approvals and completion of the agreed transaction steps. Employees in Swiss Re Corporate Solutions’ South African business are expected to join Old Mutual Insure, subject to approvals and final transaction terms. Old Mutual Insure would also become its local network partner for International Programs in South Africa, supporting South African corporates and multinational companies operating in the country.

item.title: Mitchell, Tractable Plan Automated Collision Intake Integration
item.description: The planned integration is intended to give North American multi-site operators (MSOs) and independent collision repair centers an automated path from vehicle intake and damage documentation to creation of a preliminary repair estimate. (Image source: Tractable LumaScanner page.) Mitchell (San Diego) plans to expand its collaboration with Tractable (London) through a proposed exclusive agreement connecting Tractable’s LumaScanner automated vehicle inspection system with Mitchell Intelligent Estimating. “Our goal is to help collision repairers simplify the vehicle intake process by connecting innovative technologies that are designed to optimize key steps in the workflow,” comments Olivier Baudoux, SVP, Global Product Strategy and Artificial Intelligence, Mitchell.

item.title: Amdocs Enters Insurance With $340 Million EIS Acquisition
item.description: (Image source: IIR.) Amdocs (Jersey City, N.J.) has acquired EIS (San Francisco) for approximately $340 million in cash, making its first entry into the insurance industry and establishing the sector as a strategic growth and diversification market. “The EIS acquisition gives Amdocs a credible entry into insurance, where carriers face the same legacy billing and policy challenges that Amdocs has tackled for telecom operators for decades,” comments Karlyn Carnahan, Executive Partner, Celent. “The move also reflects a clear push to diversify beyond a telecom market where growth is increasingly hard to find.” Carnahan characterizes the $340 million acquisition as “a modest, long-term bet,” adding that its success will depend on whether Amdocs can demonstrate that its telecom-developed aOS platform resonates with insurers in a crowded core-systems market.

item.title: Flarre.AI Names Sokal VP of AI and Products
item.description: (Aasim Kumar Sokal, VP, AI and Products, Flarre.AI. Source: Flarre.AI.) Flarre.AI (Tampa, Fla.) has appointed Aasim Kumar Sokal VP of AI and Products, giving him responsibility for the company’s AI, product and platform strategy. In his new role, Sokal will help translate carrier requirements and market needs into platform capabilities and identify new areas for product development as Flarre.AI expands its insurance-native agentic AI platform.

item.title: New APCIA Initiative Looks to Help ‘Backbone’ of Industry With Regulatory Costs
item.description: “Collectively they give our private competitive marketplace much of the depth, specialization and resilience that it enjoys.” However, discussions with 20 small and medium carriers on APCIA’s board confirmed there is a need to reduce regulatory costs that are amounting to what Bell described as a “scale tax” that is paid “not because the company presents more risk, but because it has fewer premium dollars across which to spread a largely fixed cost.” “Delays in approvals, filings or licensing, costly and inconsistently applied state exam formats – they don’t just cost money, they cost opportunity,” Bell said, adding that when the admitted market becomes slower, capital and product innovation migrate to the excess and surplus lines market – a “structural rather than situation” migration. APCIA’s proposed Small and Medium Sized Insurer Regulatory Cost Initiative (SMSIRCI) will work to pursue regulatory improvements and benefits for carriers that will hopefully trickle to consumers once changes positively affect the expense ratios of small and medium-sized carriers. Small and midsize carriers “form the backbone” of the private insurance market, and they are being bogged down by the cost of regulatory and corporate compliance.

item.title: The Latest Launches from Insurify, Insurity
item.description: Insurify, an online insurance marketplace, announced the launch of its AI Agent Gateway with the aim of giving consumers a faster, more efficient way to shop for insurance using their personal AI agents. The gateway connects AI agents directly to Insurify’s marketplace so a shopper’s agent can gather and compare real-time quotes while preserving information and safeguards essential to choosing coverage. The launch builds on Insurify’s introduction of a ChatGPT plugin for insurance shopping.

item.title: Crunchbase Data: Less Than 2% Of 2026 Venture Funding Went To Post-Election Red States
item.description: So far this year, less than 2% of all startup investment has gone to companies in post-election red states, defined as those that will have both a Republican governor and two Republican U.S. This year, as of Election Day, startups in the remaining 17 red states 1 , which are home to nearly a quarter of Americans, had collectively pulled in just $8.6 billion in venture funding, with Florida, Tennessee and Utah among the largest contributors. Beyond the aforementioned newcomers Texas and Ohio, several other purple states regularly pull in sizable venture funding, including Pennsylvania, North Carolina and to some extent Wisconsin.
